name: Manufacturer
description: A manufacturing company: a product catalogue with an enquiry basket, machines and equipment, references, documents to download and job openings, with facts about capacity, certifications and lead times.

questions.question: In which year was the company founded?
How many people work for you?
questions.help: A number; the site states it as a fact, so update it when it changes.

questions.question: How large is your production area in square metres?
Which certifications does the company hold?
questions.help: Only certifications you actually hold, with the standard, e.g. ISO 9001. Leave it empty if there are none.

questions.question: Which countries do you deliver to?
Is there a minimum order quantity or value?
What is the usual lead time of an order?
questions.help: For example "2–4 weeks from order confirmation".

audit.message: Add your products to the catalogue – buyers compare parameters and send an enquiry from it.
Add at least one reference project your customers have agreed to publish.
State your usual lead time – it is the first question of every buyer.
The product catalogue has not changed for a year – check prices, availability and datasheets.
Fill in the company registration number in Business details – business customers need it for their orders.
Publish your terms and conditions – business customers look for them before ordering; check what your law requires of them.

claude: Buyers on a manufacturer's site look for what is made, in which parameters and quantities, how fast it can be delivered and whom to ask – lead with the product catalogue, the lead time and a direct contact, and keep company figures (founded, employees, area, countries) as facts. Write factually and technically; a parameter table says more than adjectives. Never invent certifications, standards, customers, reference projects, capacities, tolerances or prices – every such claim must come from the owner, and a reference may be published only with the customer's agreement. Products have no checkout here: visitors collect them into an enquiry, so make the enquiry path visible on every product page. Documents (datasheets, certificates, terms) belong in the document library so that a new edition keeps its address.
